correctness.rationale: For generic affine planes of a tetrahedron, section vertex count is 3 or 4. Integrating individual edge-crossing offsets gives 2π times total edge length; integrating intersecting-plane mass gives total edge length times exterior angle. For the specified shape, three right exterior angles and three arctangent angles yield exactly the stated formula. The derivative D′=2tA/z cancels nontrivial terms; the sign reduces to an increasing A/B crossing decreasing G once at t=1. Exact endpoint limits and the two-branch inverse statement follow. Five aspect ratios independently agree with direct numerical width/edge-crossing integration; numerical tests are corroboration, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Motion-invariant random section vertex frequency is a natural coarse stereological invariant. The theorem supplies a complete nondegenerate parameter law, a rigid interior maximizer, sharp unequal degeneration behavior and a precise two-to-one inverse interval. This is a mathematically motivated shape-optimization/inverse problem rather than an arbitrary slice or a mere computation of a known table; it does not extend its claims to all tetrahedra.
